context.p: Background noise — such as hum from electronics, hiss from a microphone, or fan noise — can degrade the quality of your recordings. includes a Noise Reduction effect that can dramatically improve audio clarity.

note.p: For podcast recordings, apply noise reduction before compression and equalization. The order of effects matters: clean the audio first, then shape its dynamics and tone.

step.cmd: Identify a section of audio that contains only the background noise (no speech or desired audio).

info.p: Look for a quiet gap at the beginning or end of your recording. You need at least half a second of noise-only audio.
This captures the characteristics of the background noise. The dialog will close automatically.

step.cmd: Select the entire track by pressing Ctrl+A (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+A (macOS).
Adjust the settings and click OK.

note.p: Excessive noise reduction can make voices sound metallic or underwater. Start with moderate settings and increase gradually. Use Preview to listen before applying.

result.p: The background noise has been reduced across your entire track. Play back the audio to verify the result sounds natural.
